messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Streaming p99 latency spike detected on /v1/stream (eu-west). p95=420ms p99=4.3s error_rate=0.6% • auto-paged #incidents • runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/streaming-latency
ryan (oncall): ack — I'm on it, joining logs now
emma (sre): on the proxy tier, seeing a lot of upstream write stalls and 499s; starting grep across proxies
ryan (oncall): any immediate customer-facing impact?
maya (product): support has two reports of streaming timeouts from a single enterprise customer; most users retried and got through, but noticeable slowness for some clients
tom (support): confirmed. customer reported repeated reconnects between 12:15-12:34 UTC. collecting request ids now
jia (eng-platform): FYI I pushed a small nginx tweak at ~12:15 to reduce keepalive_timeout for a test cluster (75s -> 15s) and tightened proxy_buffer_size to free sockets faster. rolling that back now while we investigate
emma (sre): logs show repeated write errors from proxy to backend, looks like EAGAIN / resource temporarily unavailable, followed by upstream timeouts
ryan (oncall): paste a snippet of the errors?
emma (sre): ```bash
$ tail -n 5 /var/log/proxy/proxy.log | grep -i writev
[12:18:03] proxy1 writev: EAGAIN
[12:18:07] proxy2 writev: EAGAIN
[12:19:02] proxy1 upstream timeout after 10.5s
[12:20:15] proxy3 client closed connection (499)
[12:23:01] proxy2 writev: EAGAIN
```
jia (eng-platform): that matches. re-rolled nginx config at 12:28 UTC — keepalive_timeout -> 75s, restored proxy_buffer_size and proxy_busy_buffers_size, and set proxy_buffering off for the streaming route
emma (sre): metrics after revert: p99 down to ~1.1s, p95 ~380ms. still a small tail at 12:34 but much reduced
ryan (oncall): do we need to scale anything while we watch?
jia (eng-platform): spun up +1 proxy instance and bumped the backend connection pool limit to reduce head-of-line for long-lived SSEs. watching connection churn and outbound queue depth
maya (product): what's the affected window we should tell customers?
tom (support): impacted window: ~12:15 — 12:34 UTC for the main report; intermittent slowness persisted for some clients until ~12:40. I'll create the customer ticket and include timeline + mitigation steps
emma (sre): root cause hypothesis: the aggressive keepalive + smaller buffer sizes made proxies more sensitive to slow-reading clients. when a burst of slow consumers showed up, proxy sockets hit EAGAIN and proxy->upstream writes stalled, causing long tails and some upstream timeouts
ryan (oncall): mitigation checklist: 1) config revert (done) 2) +1 proxy (done) 3) monitor p99/p95 for 30m 4) open postmortem if we see recurrence
incident-bot: Incident state changed: active -> monitoring (config revert detected)
maya (product): agree on postmortem. suggest adding a staging test that simulates slow clients reading SSEs and a canary for any keepalive/buffer changes that touch streaming routes
jia (eng-platform): will open a PR tomorrow with guardrails: require streaming route toggle and automated slow-client test in CI before rolling config changes to prod
ryan (oncall): thanks team. marking paging as cleared unless new alerts come in. :thumbsup:
tom (support): filing follow-up ticket INC-2026 with timeline, impacted customers, and mitigation notes
emma (sre): leaving watch on p99 and socket EAGAINs for 1h, will escalate if anything reappears
ryan (oncall): closing the page — good job everyone
